description:
📝 Notes
Feb 11, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Amir Houieh provided updates on the Carefinder project, including creating a new Unbody version with predefined requirements and planning a meeting with Carefinder next week to finalize future strategy and quotation, in addition to finishing the desktop website and addressing mobile issues. Noémi Biró analyzed Sibil user feedback, scheduled a user meeting with Melissa, and confirmed text changes requested by Melissa for the login screen to help define Phase Two's scope. Gabor Kerekes proposed experimental work like a generative UI with LLMs and a blog post on sandboxing, while the team agreed to a soft launch of the redesigned website by the end of the day after testing across different configurations. The team also agreed to keep Discord as the primary communication channel, reserving Signal for sharing sensitive credentials, and Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes discussed restructuring the Carefinder enhancement pipeline and the importance of materializing ideas into practical experiments rather than solely sharing articles.
Details
Weekly Sync-up and Updates The meeting began with a sync-up to start the week, focusing on updates from each team member. Amir Houieh provided updates on scheduling a financial meeting with Melissa to finalize an agreement and starting the outline for that meeting, which they plan to share with the team (00:00:00). They also mentioned finishing the desktop version of the website, addressing mobile responsiveness issues based on feedback from Gabor Kerekes, and implementing the copies for the landing page and blog (00:06:12).
Carefinder Project Updates Amir Houieh shared updates on creating a new version of the Unbody product for Carefinder, emphasizing the need to get it ready for delivery. They noted some fundamental differences between the current version and Carefinder's needs, leading to the creation of a new branch with predefined requirements that passed all tests (00:07:23). Amir Houieh confirmed they are running tests with real data for this phase, and expects the project to take a few more days (00:08:32).
Future Carefinder Strategy and Quotation Amir Houieh is planning a talk with Carefinder people next week to understand their long-term needs, especially regarding future releases and specific requirements like an admin dashboard, to prepare a more customized version. This discussion is also intended to help determine the quotation and assess if more work is needed than initially expected (00:08:32).
User Feedback and User Meetings for Sibil Noémi Biró started analyzing data from Sibil to understand user feedback. They scheduled their first user meeting with Melissa for that afternoon, focusing on a specific user who had a role at Headspace, to better prepare questions related to that user's perspective on Sibil (00:09:34).
Sibil Text Changes and Phase Two Scope Noémi Biró mentioned that Melissa requested slowly changing the text, starting with the login screen. They confirmed that they should be able to make this change by pulling the latest from GitHub and opening a pull request for Gabor Kerekes to deploy. Noémi Biró also stressed the importance of these user inputs for defining the scope of Phase Two (00:10:54).
Gabor Kerekes' Proposed Experimental Work Gabor Kerekes presented their ideas for work, including drafting articles for the blog and exploring experimental work such as connecting their Unison experiment to an LLM to explore a generative UI idea. This experiment aims to see if the LLM can be used as a mechanism for quickly building apps, similar to a V-coding platform (00:12:34).
Discussion on Sandboxing and Experimentation Gabor Kerekes discussed writing a blog post about sandboxing, sharing the setup, and open-sourcing it (00:12:34). Amir Houieh noted that while the sandbox's structure works well, its limitations include not being able to run Docker or execute code. Gabor Kerekes explained that the sandbox's main benefit is security, allowing the use of the `dangerously skip permissions` flag to grant full autonomy within a confined virtual machine (00:14:32). They suggested this approach allows multiple agents to run in parallel on different ideas without risk (00:16:06).
Prioritizing Experiments and External Outcomes Amir Houieh encouraged experimentation like the sandbox, but emphasized the need for a defined timeline and budget to avoid over-complication (00:17:26). They reiterated the importance of shipping and having an outcome for the outside world, suggesting that Gabor Kerekes could dedicate a specific period, like a week, to the sandbox project (00:18:18). Gabor Kerekes agreed, focusing on the blog post as a means of interacting with the outside world and establishing an online presence (00:19:16).
Website Blog Post Strategy and Review Gabor Kerekes suggested reviewing the website and blog posts to ensure relevance and a good signal-to-noise ratio (00:19:16) (00:23:32). Amir Houieh proposed removing non-relevant or business-oriented articles but leaving those that drive traffic based on analytics. Gabor Kerekes agreed to review the articles, identifying traffic-driving posts to keep and determining which non-relevant ones to retire or archive (00:22:33) (00:24:48).
Website Design and Implementation Review Amir Houieh shared a look at the current website design, including links to GitHub and hello.io, the manifesto in the "lab" section, and the blog with a small animation and filters for topics (00:26:07). Noémi Biró gave positive feedback on the categories and the overall implementation, but questioned a distracting dot after the blog link, which Amir Houieh agreed to remove. Gabor Kerekes noted that the website was being pushed to the main branch (00:27:17).
Website Testing and Launch Plans The team confirmed the website link was shared on Discord for testing and that a new deployment included fixes for mobile issues. Gabor Kerekes experienced slow loading on mobile, while Noémi Biró noted quicker loading but slow navigation (00:28:23) (00:31:04). Noémi Biró also observed the website in dark mode, suggesting testing for this configuration (00:29:58). Gabor Kerekes proposed focusing on website testing and review for the day, ensuring functionality across different browsers and operating systems, and reviewing articles with the analytics Amir Houieh would provide. They decided on a soft launch of the website by the end of the day (00:32:42).
Sharing Analytics Access Amir Houieh planned to share analytics screenshots or the password for the hello@onbody.io account with the team using Signal's disappearing messages (00:34:07). Gabor Kerekes guided Noémi Biró on using Mac OS's built-in password manager to safely store the credentials (00:37:37).
Communication Channel Agreement The team discussed their primary communication channel, concluding that Discord should remain the central location for work communications. Signal would be reserved for sensitive topics like credential sharing, to prevent scattering important information across multiple platforms (00:40:58).
Carefinder Enhancement Pipeline Restructuring Amir Houieh explained the necessary restructuring of the Carefinder enhancement pipeline, which was previously misconceptualized as a separate endpoint (00:40:58). They created a new milestone to integrate the enhancer into the VIV pipeline while ensuring it could still function in isolation, addressing previous issues. Amir Houieh noted that the agent is working on eval cases, but must run Cloud outside the sandbox for these due to the sandbox's inability to run Docker (00:42:07).
Agent Autonomy and Permissions Gabor Kerekes advised Amir Houieh on using the less-secure-but-sufficient slash command sandbox built into Cloud for situations outside the VM to grant some autonomy without constant supervision (00:42:07). They emphasized the importance of only using the `dangerously skip permissions` flag inside the VM (00:43:51). Gabor Kerekes also confirmed that Amir Houieh's phase one changes would be pushed with the automatic commit feature (00:45:00).
Future Simplification of VIV Pipeline Gabor Kerekes suggested that using VIV8's embedded mode, which allows it to run in the same process as the server, could simplify the application, similar to how SQLite works (00:45:00). Amir Houieh agreed to look into this depending on the scale (00:46:26).
Discussion on Self-Evolving Memory Architecture Gabor Kerekes highlighted recent research on self-evolving memory systems, where LLMs can determine the optimal memory architecture for different use cases (00:47:25). They posited that this concept of applying machine learning to memory systems could be relevant to the team's "brain" or Nexus architecture (00:48:24). Amir Houieh agreed that this is interesting but reiterated that the LLM still needs tools and options to act as the orchestrator (00:50:14).
Feedback on Exploration vs. Shipping Amir Houieh shared a concern that Gabor Kerekes seemed more excited about other people's work and too critical of the team's internal work, potentially hindering enthusiasm and the drive to ship products (00:52:46). Amir Houieh expressed a desire to see Gabor Kerekes build upon internal work, rather than just sending articles, to show alignment and accelerate the shipping process (00:56:41). Gabor Kerekes countered that their motivation is to explore and curate the best ideas, not to criticize or create anxiety about being left behind (00:58:49). They acknowledged the validity of getting stuck in exploration and recognized the difference in their approaches, with Amir Houieh preferring to quickly sketch out ideas after minimal exploration (01:00:11).
Strategy for Idea Sharing Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh discussed improving how they share ideas, concluding that presenting concepts in the context of a practical experiment is better than just sending articles, although articles are still acceptable with a need for balance (01:01:06). Amir Houieh expressed that practical examples, like what Gabor Kerekes did with Unison, would be much more effective if materialized into something like a generative UI. Amir Houieh emphasized the importance of action, noting a desire to keep relevant and avoid ideas being implemented by others (01:02:06).
Materializing Ideas The speakers agreed on the need to materialize more of their ideas, even if it's just a one-day prototype, to keep pace and bring their concepts to fruition. Amir Houieh recalled a past frustration from a third year where there was excessive debate and talking without practical creation, underscoring the shift toward tangible results. Gabor Kerekes acknowledged the shared history of being frustrated and agreed to move forward with practical work, appreciating the necessity of these challenges (01:02:53).
Suggested next steps
Amir Houieh will work on the outline today and tomorrow and then share it with the group for review before the fin meeting to finalize the agreement.
Amir Houieh will have a talk with Carefinder people next week to understand their long-term needs, including whether Alex needs an admin dashboard, to inform a more custom version and quotation.
Noémi Biró will prepare for the first user meeting this afternoon at 5 with Melissa by researching the user's role in Headspace to understand her perspective and ask relevant questions about Sibil.
Gabor Kerekes will focus on the website today, including testing and review, ensuring it works well in Android, iOS, and Firefox, and review the articles after Amir Houieh sends the analytics.
Amir Houieh will test the website on actual phones to reproduce the issues with mobile tap behavior, then push the changes, and look into adding dark mode.
Amir Houieh will push the completed phase one code for Carefinder and look into using VV8's embedded mode to simplify the solution.
Noémi Biró will implement the requested text change in the login screen by pulling the latest from GitHub, and then open a pull request for Gabor Kerekes to deploy it.
Amir Houieh will send the analytics to Gabor Kerekes so he can identify which articles are driving traffic for the blog review and determine if others should be retired or archived.
Gabor Kerekes will write a blog post about sandboxing, share the setup as open source, and explore the impact of using LLMs within a secure sandbox for building prototypes and exploring ideas in parallel.
Amir Houieh will share the password for the hello@onbody.io account in a disappearing message on the Signal R&D group with Noémi Biró and Gabor Kerekes so they can access the analytics and add the account to their browsers.
Amir Houieh will work on the memory the brain again.
Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes will have a separate meeting to discuss the Carefinder project.
Gabor Kerekes will present anything interesting he finds in the context of a practical experiment instead of just sending an article.
Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh will materialize more of the ideas they are talking about, even if it's just a one day prototype.
